# Glossary of Terms

A concise, definitive reference for Nix and NixOS terminology.

### Derivation (`.drv`)
The fundamental build specification in Nix. A derivation is an immutable file in the `/nix/store` describing exactly which inputs, tools, environment variables, and build scripts are required to produce an output artifact.

### Nix Store (`/nix/store`)
The cryptographic, content-addressable filesystem where all packages, configurations, and build products reside. Paths are uniquely identified by a 32-character base32 hash derived from their inputs or contents.

### Closure
The complete, self-contained set of all store paths required to run an application or boot an operating system. A closure has zero implicit external dependencies.

### Flake
A standardized file layout centered on `flake.nix` and `flake.lock` that provides hermetic evaluation, explicit input pinning, and standardized outputs across all Nix repositories without global state.

### DevShell
A temporary, isolated shell environment created by `nix develop` or `nix-shell` containing exactly the compilers, libraries, and tools specified for a project.

### Binary Cache / Substituter
An HTTP service (such as `cache.nixos.org`, Cachix, or Attic) serving pre-compiled store closures. When Nix requires a store path, it queries substituters before compiling from source.

### Garbage Collection Root (GC Root)
A symlink outside the Nix store (such as `/run/current-system` or `result`) that protects a store path and its entire dependency closure from being deleted by `nix-collect-garbage`.

### Home Manager
A declarative user-environment management system using Nix modules to configure user-space dotfiles, shell environments, and user applications.

### Overlay
A Nix function with signature `final: prev: { ... }` used to modify, override, or extend packages in `nixpkgs` without editing upstream files.

### Module System
The extensible configuration engine powering NixOS and Home Manager. Modules define typed `options` and assign `config` values that merge deterministically across multiple files.
